papers.title: The 120-Cell Dissected by the Hyperplanes of Its Final Stellation: the golden ring Z[phi] as foundation, from Kramer's seven cells to 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits
papers.abstract: The diagonals of a regular pentagon dissect it into eleven pieces and draw a pentagram; the dodecahedron dissected by the twelve face planes of its inner core gives Kramer's seven "elementary cells" of 1982. We define the stellation dissection of a golden regular polytope in any dimension as the dissection of the convex hull of its final regular stellation by the facet hyperplanes of the core, show that the core has phi^(-d) of the inradius of the hull for d = 2, 3, 4, and carry the dissection out for the first time on the 120-cell. The foundation is the arithmetic of the golden ring Z[phi], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt 5): vertices and hyperplanes live in Z[phi]^d, every orientation test is the exact sign of an element of Z[phi], decided with integers, and the pieces are named by sign vectors. We develop this foundation from scratch (conjugation, norm, units, the primes sqrt 5, 2, 3, the exact sign test, the lattice x -> (x, conj x), the vertex modules of the dodecahedron and the 120-cell, the icosian ring) and let it carry the geometry. The definition bifurcates in dimension four: the star cut at depth phi^(-4), a unit, has 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits of H4; the hereditary cut at depth 1 - phi^(-4) = sqrt 5 / phi^2, a unit times the ramified prime, induces the three-dimensional dissection on every facet and has 8,161 cells in 8 orbits. New here: all vertices of the dodecahedral and of the hereditary dissection lie in the vertex module of the polytope being cut, whereas the star cut needs the denominators 2, 3 and 5; the seven kinds of pieces of the dodecahedron are exactly the I_h-orbits of sign vectors, with stellation layer equal to the number of plus signs. We catalogue the four-dimensional pieces and treat the circumscribed disc, ball and 4-ball. Every number quoted is recomputed exactly by a script whose output is reproduced in an appendix.

papers.title: Magic Gems: Convex Hulls of Lifted Magic Squares
papers.abstract: Given an arrangement of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ in an $n\times n$ grid, we lift each cell to $\mathbb{R}^3$ by centring its grid coordinates $(x,y)$ at the origin and taking its centred entry $z = s_{ij} - (n^2+1)/2$ as a vertical height. The convex hull of these $n^2$ points is the gem of the arrangement, whose lower and upper boundaries are the regular subdivisions of the grid induced by $\pm z$. While random arrangements and generic linear magic squares have gems whose vertex counts grow with $n$, our main theorem shows that the classical Siamese (de la Loub\`ere) magic square of every odd order $n\ge5$ has $f$-vector $(12,26,16)$, isometry group $\{\pm\mathrm{id}\}$, and only the twelve vertices forced by the boundary of the grid. The proof shears the lift onto five horizontal terraces and reduces the hull calculation to a finite table of polynomials in $m=(n-1)/2$; the same method gives $f$-vector $(12,24,14)$ for the base-$n$ digit-exchanged square. Along any family of linear squares with fixed steps the $f$-vector is eventually periodic in $n$, whereas over all linear magic squares of prime order $n$ the maximum vertex count grows as $\Theta(\ln n)$. Whenever the heights have vanishing first moments, a short principal-axes argument shows that the point set has a non-trivial isometry if and only if the arrangement is self-complementary up to dihedral symmetry. An exact census of the $880$ magic squares of order four yields $616$ congruence classes and $352$ combinatorial types of gems, and shows that while vertex and facet counts are nearly insensitive to the magic line-sum conditions, the volume and solid centroid shift systematically.

papers.title: Formalizing the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes by a Generalized Notion of Co-dimension
papers.abstract: In this work, we formalize the concept of intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes introduced in Li et al. (2018), which measures the structural complexity of learning problems by training along randomly generated subspaces. We define the intrinsic dimension of a set $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^p$ as the minimal dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(\Theta)$ such that a random plane of dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(\Theta)$ in $\mathbb{R}^p$ intersects $\Theta$ with probability one. We show that it is a generalized notion of co-dimension that depends on the global geometry of $\Theta$. We study mathematical properties of the intrinsic dimension and develop techniques to estimate the intrinsic dimension of sets $\Theta$ that arise in learning problems. More specifically, we derive upper and/or lower bounds where $\Theta$ is the set of optimal parameters in student-teacher settings with shallow and deep ReLU networks, including finite and infinite sample cases, and with and without regularization. We discuss how our theory leads to novel types of generalization bounds, thereby showing that the intrinsic dimension is a measure of learning complexity. Our results connect techniques from seemingly different areas of machine learning research such as classification of symmetries of ReLU networks and stochastic geometry.

papers.title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.

papers.title: The generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, including rigidity in the equality case. As a corollary, we obtain that isoperimetric regions are bounded. We prove the conjecture for Alexandrov spaces with two sided curvature bounds as well. A sharp Michael-Simon-type inequality for hypersurfaces in these spaces is also shown.

papers.title: Gel'fand's inverse problem under Ricci curvature bounds
papers.abstract: The classical Gel'fand's inverse problem asks whether a Riemannian manifold is uniquely determined by the knowledge of the heat kernel on any open subset of the manifold. We study this inverse problem in the non-smooth setting in the framework of ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, namely, metric-measure spaces with synthetic Riemannian Ricci curvature bounded below by $K$ and dimension bounded above by $N$. We establish the unique solvability of Gel'fand's inverse problem for the class of compact ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces whose regular set admits Lipschitz Riemannian structure. As an application, we obtain the continuity of Gel'fand's inverse problem in the class of closed Riemannian manifolds with bounded Ricci curvature, diameter and volume bounded from below. We note that the results are new even for Einstein orbifolds and (weighted) Lipschitz Riemannian manifolds with non-smooth boundary.

papers.title: Sobolev Inequalities Relating Rough Riemannian Metrics to their Distance Functions
papers.abstract: In previous papers, the first named author and E. Bryden explored Sobolev like inequalities relating the norm of a Riemmanian metric $g_1$, in terms of a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, in order to estimate the distance function $d_{g_1}$. Although $|g_1|_{g_0}$ is not the gradient of the distance function $d_{g_1}$, it was shown that a Morrey and Sobolev inequalities hold in their appropriate domains. In this paper we see that these results can be extended to the case where $g_1$ is a Rough Riemannian metric, something roughly analogous to an $L^{\infty}$ metric. We show that the proof of the Morrey and Sobolev inequality go through, with appropriate adjustments, as well as convergence results. We also adapt previous examples from the literature to the rough Riemannian metric case which show the hypotheses from the main theorems are necessary.

papers.title: Carnot geodesics with H\"older controls
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit length-minimizing curve in a polynomial rank-two sub-Riemannian structure on $\R^4$. Its arclength parametrization is $C^{1,1/2}$ and is not $C^{1,\alpha}$ near an interior point for any $\alpha>1/2$. Minimality is proved by an approximate calibration chosen separately for each competitor. The example admits a minimizing lift to a rank-two Carnot group of step five. Generalizations are announced.

papers.title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
papers.abstract: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.

papers.title: Johnson optimality and uniqueness for distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$
papers.abstract: We prove that a two-distance set in $\mathbb R^d$ with distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$ has at most $d(d+1)/2$ points for every $d\ge9$. Equality in full affine dimension characterizes the Johnson construction; for $d\ge10$, the full-dimensional condition is automatic. The proof separates configurations according to the connectivity of the short-distance graph. The connected case uses root lattices and intersection theorems, while the disconnected case uses an orthogonal decomposition into component direction spaces and the span of their center differences. We also prove a relative bound for Euclidean two-distance sets and show that equality forces sphericity. Together with the Larman--Rogers--Seidel theorem, these results give maximum cardinality $d(d+1)/2$ for $9\le d\le21$ and $275$ for $d=22$, without exhaustive enumeration.

papers.title: Maximum Diversity and Support Transitions on Disks and Three-Dimensional Balls
papers.abstract: For the similarity kernel $e^{-|x-y|}$, we determine the probability measure of maximum diversity on every planar disk and three-dimensional ball, answering a question of Leinster and Roff. In each dimension the measure is uniform on the boundary up to a threshold. Above it, the support is a closed central ball and the outer sphere, separated by a mass-free annulus. In dimensions two and three, their conjecture of finitely many supporting spheres therefore holds only up to the respective threshold. We obtain the measure explicitly up to one scalar root in three dimensions and through Fredholm integral equations and a scalar contact equation in the plane. Computations in dimensions four and five suggest that interior supporting spheres appear one at a time.

papers.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
papers.abstract: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichm\"uller spaces. We further establish large deviation principles for quasimorphisms on countable groups, and for random walks generated by compositions of Euclidean isometries; also, we discuss extensions and streamlining of known large deviation results for singular values of random matrix products. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.

papers.title: Borsuk number in four dimensions is at most seven
papers.abstract: We prove that every bounded set of diameter one in four-dimensional Euclidean space can be covered by seven balls of diameter strictly smaller than $0.9999$. In particular, the Borsuk number satisfies $b_4\le7$. The proof combines geometric arguments based on contact points of the circumball with an exact finite computation. For small and large circumradius, the covering centres are constructed analytically. In the remaining range, a suitable triangle of contact points reduces the problem to a four-parameter family of ball polytopes. The parameter cube is subdivided into 23494 boxes. For each parameter box, candidate centres are found by nonlinear optimization, and the resulting covering is verified using exact rational interval arithmetic and paraboloid lifting.

papers.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
papers.abstract: Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and R\'enyi entropy. We first establish several bounds for the energy, and then discuss the monotonicity, measure invariance of the dimensions, as well as some concrete graph families.

papers.title: Lipschitz volume rigidity for non-collapsed $\rm RCD$ spaces with boundary
papers.abstract: We study Lipschitz-volume rigidity for non-collapsed ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, possibly with boundary. We prove that a measure-preserving $1$-Lipschitz map between such spaces restricts to an isometry from the interior of the domain onto its image, where the latter is equipped with the intrinsic length distance. We then characterize when this interior rigidity extends to an isometric bijection between the whole spaces, in terms of the behavior of the map on the boundaries. Along the way, we establish a rigidity result of independent interest in a more general class of rectifiable metric spaces.

papers.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
papers.abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.

papers.title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
papers.abstract: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
papers.abstract: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric. We prove that when $\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact connected embedded submanifold without boundary, with positive reach, and $\mathrm{A}\subset\mathcal{M}$ is a subset that is sufficiently dense in $\mathcal{M}$ with respect to the reach, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is bounded below by $1/2$ of the Hausdorff distance between them. We extend this result in two ways. First, we show that the factor $1/2$ can be improved using Jung's theorem. Second, we prove bounds on the Gromov-Hausdorff distance for pairs of subsets of $\mathcal{M}$. When $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ is equipped with the two-dimensional Euclidean metric, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ and any sufficiently dense subset of $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ can be expressed explicitly as a function of the Hausdorff distance between the two. We use interleavings between geometric simplicial complexes, nerve lemmas, properties of reach and the nearest-point projection map, and the fundamental class to produce the inequalities for general $\mathcal{M}$. We use the Borsuk-Ulam theorem for $\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{S}^1\subset \mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $\lambda$-convex bodies
papers.abstract: For a given $\lambda > 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $\lambda$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/\lambda$. We show that among all $\lambda$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $\lambda$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/\lambda$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $\lambda > 0$.

papers.title: The point-cross dimension
papers.abstract: Two transverse segments have local Hausdorff and upper box dimension one at their crossing, although they carry two independent tangent directions. We define the Point-Cross Dimension by assigning each tangent line the largest local upper box dimension captured by intersection with a regular \(C^1\) curve in that direction, then taking the supremum of their sums over finite independent families of tangent lines. Every Bouligand direction admits such a recurrent curve. The resulting profile is invariant under closure and covariant under local \(C^1\)-diffeomorphisms. Each directional weight is attained, and the profile is upper semicontinuous. An integral representation by ranks of weight superlevel sets gives submodularity and, together with projection bounds, exact Cartesian-product additivity. Germs with the same projective tangent support, local upper box dimension, and rank of segment directions can have different Point-Cross Dimensions. Further computations give exact directional profiles for chirps and the Point-Cross Dimension of a self-affine carpet. Finally, approximation of a ray with error \(O(t^d)\), for \(d>1\), forces directional weight at least \(1-1/d\), and this bound is sharp.

papers.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
papers.abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollob\'as and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Guti\'errez, Bernu\'es, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollob\'as and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.

papers.title: Quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products
papers.abstract: We provide obstructions to the existence of quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products of trees, hyperbolic spaces, and other right-angled Artin groups.

papers.title: Solution of Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem
papers.abstract: In 1991, Laczkovich asked whether every measurable set of positive measure in $\mathbb R^d$ can be mapped onto a cube with a Lipschitz map. We show that the answer is positive for every $d$. Our results also give a positive answer for Kolmogorov's problem on contractions onto polygons with small measure loss in the case of Jordan measurable sets.

papers.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
papers.abstract: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

papers.title: The Discrete Monotonicity Property in Rank Two
papers.abstract: The Betke--Henk--Wills conjecture predicts a bound for lattice-point counts in terms of successive minima. Malikiosis introduced the discrete monotonicity property for normalized residue counts as a sufficient condition for this bound and its extension to nonsymmetric convex bodies. We prove that every compact convex set satisfies this property for lattice subgroups of rank at most two, in arbitrary ambient dimension.

papers.title: On $\kappa$-covering minima
papers.abstract: We introduce $\kappa$-covering minima by requiring the permutation simplices of one independent lattice frame to fit into translates of a common dilate of a convex body. We prove a lower bound for their normalized product, with coefficient $(n+1)/2^n$ for centrally symmetric bodies and an explicit dependence on Minkowski asymmetry in general. On Euclidean balls, the supremum over full-rank lattices of the ratio of the resulting fitting radius to the covering radius has order $\sqrt n$. We also establish basic comparisons with classical lattice minima and bounds under products, projections, Minkowski addition, and free direct sums. We extend the definition by allowing projected periodic lattice triangulations. These extended minima agree with the classical covering minima on ellipsoids.

papers.title: The measure contraction property and rectifiability
papers.abstract: We show that a metric measure space $(X,d,\mathfrak{m})$ with finite upper $N$-density that satisfies $\mathsf{MCP}(K,N)$ is $N$-rectifiable. This removes a unique tangent requirement from arXiv:2505.01151.

papers.title: Almost Homogeneity Characterizes Almost Bi-Lipschitz Euclidean Embeddability
papers.abstract: A metric space admits an almost bi-Lipschitz embedding into a Euclidean space if and only if it is almost homogeneous. We prove the sufficient direction, complementing the known necessary condition. More quantitatively, we bound the target dimension and the embedding constants for every logarithmic exponent $\gamma>1$. The bounds depend only on the covering parameters in the almost homogeneity condition. In particular every doubling metric space admits such an embedding. This answers a question of Margaris and Robinson and the almost bi-Lipschitz part of a question of Olson and Robinson. As a consequence, the difference set of the image is doubling, which answers the difference-set questions of Olson and Robinson and of Margaris.

papers.title: Coarse embeddability, $L^1$-compression and Percolations on General Graphs
papers.abstract: We show that a locally finite, connected graph has a coarse embedding into a Hilbert space if and only if there exist bond percolations with arbitrarily large marginals and two-point function vanishing at infinity. We further show that the decay of the two-point function is stretched exponential with stretching exponent $\alpha\in[0,1]$ if and only if the $L^1$-compression exponent of the graph is at least $\alpha$, leading to a probabilistic characterization of this exponent. These results are new even in the particular setting of Cayley graphs of finitely generated groups. The proofs build on new probabilistic methods introduced recently by the authors to study group-invariant percolation on Cayley graphs [28,29], which are now extended to the general, non-symmetric situation of graphs to study their coarse embeddability and $L^1$-compression exponents.

papers.title: Categorical Tiling Theory: Constructing Directed Planar Tilings via Edge Reversal
papers.abstract: Tilings of the plane resemble the simplicial and other complexes from algebraic topology, but have not been studied from this perspective. We construct finite categories corresponding to polygons with labeled directed edges, and introduce the problem of modeling tilings of the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane as presheaves over such a category. Combinatorially, this amounts to choosing an ``alignment'' for a tiling: a direction for every edge and consistent labels for the edges of each polygonal tile. We show that for a fixed tiling, given a single alignment we can characterize every other alignment of the same tiling by comparison of the edge directions. We then construct a ``reflective'' alignment for any tiling with an even number of polygons at each vertex, and from this generate a large family of alignments with elegant symmetry properties.
